faqs.question: Can I build the whole thing on my phone, or do I need a laptop?
faqs.answer: A phone is enough — the builder runs in the browser and the templates are designed for touch. A laptop only helps if you are typing a long letter or uploading several photos at once.

faqs.question: What counts as a usable photo for one of these templates?
faqs.answer: Anything where his face fills a reasonable part of the frame, including a video-call screenshot. Templates crop to a square, so a group shot with him in the back row will lose him entirely.

faqs.question: Does it cost anything to make one of these pages?
faqs.answer: We cannot confirm current pricing — the pricing block in our own facts file is empty and we will not print a figure we have not verified. Check the template list on the site for what each format currently includes.

faqs.question: My boyfriend does not take jokes well. Which of these three is safest?
faqs.answer: None of them, honestly. All three are built as parodies, and a 2025 study found that even casual jokes still register as violations, just milder ones — so pick a straight romantic format instead.

faqs.question: What do I actually write in the demands on a mock legal notice?
faqs.answer: Small, specific, true things: unreplied voice notes, stolen hoodies, a promised film you never watched. Keep every demand petty — a real grievance dressed as a joke stops being funny on the first line.

faqs.question: How many photos does the streaming-style format need?
faqs.answer: Three to five is enough to fill the catalogue rows without the page looking sparse. Fewer than three and the browse screen reads as empty, which is the part of the parody people notice.

faqs.question: Do I have to finish it in one sitting?
faqs.answer: No — the builder saves as you go, and on the most-built romantic page the median gap between first save and last edit is 6.2 hours across 1,125 pages. Most people start it, step away, and come back.

faqs.question: Is a gift maker the same thing as an e-gift-card site?
faqs.answer: No. A gift card site sells you a code redeemable somewhere else; a gift maker produces a page that exists only for him and has nothing to redeem.

faqs.question: Can I make one for a boyfriend who is not in India?
faqs.answer: Yes — the output is a public URL, so it opens anywhere with a browser and no account. Time zones matter more than geography if you are aiming for midnight.

faqs.question: What happens if I pick the wrong template halfway through?
faqs.answer: Start the other one; nothing carries over between formats, but the photos and lines you have written are already on your phone. It costs you the typing, not the material.

faqs.question: Does he need to know it is a joke before he opens it?
faqs.answer: No, and the reveal is most of the gift — the formats announce themselves within a screen or two. Only warn him first if the deadpan framing could genuinely land as bad news.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Online Gift Maker for BF: What You Need, and What Comes Out

An online gift maker for bf is a browser page that builds a page. You pick a format, drop in a photo and a few lines, and it hands you back a link you paste into WhatsApp.

The scale underneath it is deliberately small. SubhSandesh has 3,377 registered creators averaging 1.29 pages each, and a created page collects 11.5 views on average — both measured 2026-09-15.

So this is not a broadcast. It is a thing one person makes, one person opens, and a few others get shown on a phone screen later.

Below: what a maker actually is, the three things to have ready before you open one, how long the build really takes, what comes out at the end, and the check to run before you send it.

## What an online gift maker actually is

An online gift maker is a template-driven builder. The layout, the animation and the logic already exist; you supply the personal parts — his name, a photo, a handful of lines — and the tool assembles the rest.

What you get back is not a file. It is a URL that renders the finished page in his browser, which is why there is nothing for him to install and nothing for you to export.

That is the whole mechanical difference from design software. Across the 4,357 pages built on SubhSandesh since 2026-03-12, the artefact being handed over has always been a link, never a download.

## What you need in hand before you open one

Three things, and that is the entire list: one usable photo, one detail only the two of you know, and roughly half an hour where nobody needs anything from you.

The photo is where most builds stall. A screenshot from a video call works fine; a group photo with him in the back row does not, because templates crop to a square and you will lose his face.

The private detail is doing the real work. A 2020 study of product personalisation with Sri Lankan consumers found that attachment came from the *maker's own involvement* — self-expression, enjoyment, memory — rather than from customisation as such ([Fernando and Ranasinghe, FARU 2020](https://dl.lib.uom.lk/items/d3e13cc8-ea98-4212-8ae3-86d2e74ca0b1)).

Which means the nickname only he uses beats any amount of picking fonts.

## Three makers built for a boyfriend, and all three are jokes

Here the boyfriend case diverges from the girlfriend one, and the data does not prove what people assume. Our database records which *template* was opened, not who received it, so a romantic page's count says nothing about the recipient's gender.

What does transfer is register. Three SubhSandesh formats are written as jokes rather than love letters, and for a lot of boyfriends that is the difference between a page he screenshots and a page he closes.

### 1. LoveFlix — a streaming service with one show on it

A parody streaming home page where he is the lead: you browse the catalogue of your relationship, then play a branching episode. It is a send-up of an interface he opens most nights, so the joke does not need explaining.

- **You supply:** three to five photos, captions, and episode titles.
- **Build time:** the longest of the three — the catalogue rows want filling.
- **Best when:** you have a lot of photos and a shared watching habit.

### 2. The Court of Love — a trial with a penguin judge

You put him on trial in the cutest possible way: ten funny questions, a penguin presiding, and a signed stamp paper if he wins the case. The verdict is the gift, which is also why it survives being forwarded into a group chat.

- **You supply:** ten questions and one verdict line.
- **Build time:** the shortest of the three — the questions are prompted.
- **Best when:** he argues for fun and would enjoy winning.

### 3. Legal Notice — a mock notice served on your person

A formal notice served on him, in which he must accept or contest every demand, with seven days to comply. It is the driest of the three and lands hardest on someone who deals with real paperwork for a living.

- **You supply:** four to six demands and his full name.
- **Build time:** short, once you know what the demands are.
- **Best when:** his humour is deadpan rather than sentimental.

One caution, and it is the one that decides whether this works. A 2025 cross-cultural study (N = 160) found casual jokes were rated funnier, more amusing, more understandable and **less violating** than dark jokes, and dark jokes only registered as funny when the participant understood them ([Umam and colleagues, IACCP 2025](https://scholarworks.gvsu.edu/iaccp_papers/329)).

So keep the demands petty. "Failure to reply to voice notes" is funny; a real grievance is not.

If you want the joke register without the build question, the companion post on [what to send a bf when the tone is casual](https://subhsandesh.in/blog/virtual-gift-for-bf) works through the formats themselves.

## What the three cost you, in time and in material

This compares the three joke makers against the most-built romantic format on the platform.

| Maker | What you supply | Rough build time | Where it sits in 4,357 builds (2026-09-15) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [LoveFlix](https://subhsandesh.in/loveflix) | 3–5 photos, captions, episode titles | One sitting, the longest of the three | Outside the top five page types |
| [The Court of Love](https://subhsandesh.in/court-of-love) | 10 questions, 1 verdict line | Shortest — questions are prompted | Outside the top five page types |
| [Legal Notice](https://subhsandesh.in/legal-notice) | 4–6 demands, his full name | Short once the demands are decided | Outside the top five page types |
| "I love you" page | 1 photo, 1 letter | Median 6.2 hours, first save to last edit (n=1,125) | 1,125 pages, 25.8% of all builds |

The takeaway is not that the joke formats are better. It is that they are rare, which is exactly why he has not been sent one before.

## How long it really takes, and why your estimate is wrong

The typing is ten minutes. The finishing is not: on the most-built romantic page, the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.2 hours, sampled across 1,125 pages. People start it, put the phone down, and come back to it.

That gap is not abandonment. 94.1% of started pages are published and shared — 4,098 of 4,357 — so almost everyone who begins one does send it.

Two findings explain the mismatch between "ten minutes" and six hours. People routinely underestimate completion times, and across four experiments, planning *backwards* from the finished page produced longer and less biased predictions than planning forwards ([Wiese, Buehler and Griffin, Judgment and Decision Making, March 2016](https://journal.sjdm.org/16/16101/jdm16101.html)).

Separately, the amount of time you think you have inflates how big you think the job is: longer time limits produced higher completion-time estimates even when the limit was known to be arbitrary ([Goswami and Urminsky, November 2020](https://journal.sjdm.org/19/190918a/jdm190918a.html)). "I have all evening" is what makes this feel like a project.

There is a reason to push through anyway. The attachment that personalisation study measured came from the maker's own involvement rather than from how polished the finished object was — which means the part you get out of this only exists if you complete it. A finished rough page beats an unfinished neat one, and not only in his eyes.

## What comes out, and the check to run before you send it

What comes out is a link. Nothing downloads, nothing installs, he needs no account, and the page lives wherever the maker hosts it rather than on your phone.

Open that link on your own phone before he does. 49.0% of shared page views happen on a phone — 24,493 of 49,968 — so the phone rendering is the one that matters, not the desktop preview you built it in.

Then four checks, in this order: his name spelled the way *he* spells it; the photo not cropped to his shoulder; every joke demand petty rather than pointed; and a password on the page if it is going to a shared or family phone.

On cost: we cannot confirm current pricing from our own data — the pricing block in our internal facts file is empty, so we will not print a figure we have not verified. Check the [full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) for what each format currently includes.

## When an online gift maker is the wrong call for your bf

If he is in the same room, hand him something. A link is for the 2,000 km, not the two metres.

If he genuinely dislikes being the subject of a joke, none of these three is the answer — "less violating" is not the same as "not violating", and the study above is measuring degree, not absence. Pick a straight format, or write him a letter.

If the moment is heavy, a mock notice is the wrong instrument. The apology dashboard is 1,043 pages and 23.9% of everything built here, so the site does carry that weight — but in a format designed for it, not a parody of a summons.

And if his phone is old, his data is patchy, or he opens links three days late, a page that depends on an animation loading is a worse bet than a voice note. That is a mismatch with the recipient, not a failure of the maker.

## Sources

- Fernando, G.N.S. and Ranasinghe, W.M.N.D., ["Product personalization: stimulating attachment between product and consumers"](https://dl.lib.uom.lk/items/d3e13cc8-ea98-4212-8ae3-86d2e74ca0b1), FARU 2020 Proceedings, University of Moratuwa — 6 November 2020.
- Wiese, J., Buehler, R. and Griffin, D., ["Backward planning: Effects of planning direction on predictions of task completion time"](https://journal.sjdm.org/16/16101/jdm16101.html), *Judgment and Decision Making* 11(2) — March 2016.
- Goswami, I. and Urminsky, O., ["More time, more work: How time limits bias estimates of task scope and project duration"](https://journal.sjdm.org/19/190918a/jdm190918a.html), *Judgment and Decision Making* 15(6) — November 2020.
- Umam, A.N., Rusliyanti, R.O. and Oktaviani, F.R., ["Norms Violation and Dark Personality: Benign Violation Theory for Humor and Dark Humor"](https://scholarworks.gvsu.edu/iaccp_papers/329), IACCP Congress Proceedings — November 2025.

SubhSandesh figures come from the platform's own database, measured 2026-09-15. Abstracts and landing-page records were read for each cited paper; full PDFs were not retrieved.
